title: Highland Paranormal investigation group to host Halloween fundraiser
excerpt: The group will also host a huge event in Strathpeffer next month.
content:
A Highland group which investigates paranormal activity in the region will host a Halloween fundraiser.

Highland Paranormal carries out their curiosity in Highland, Moray and Aberdeenshire and has been doing so since 2010.

With Halloween imminent, the group are preparing for “the night where the veil between the dead and the living is at its thinnest”.

On Halloween itself, members the group will conduct a ‘ghost walk’ around the city in search of paranormal activity.

The main event is tonight’s (October 30) fundraiser for The Old High Inverness building at 7pm.

Team leader Liam Shand explained the significance of the location.

He said: “It's Inverness's oldest building. Part of the tower is older than Abertarff House, so it's historically probably the most important building.

“The Old High charity pulled together to save the building for the future of Inverness, but they obviously have to raise funds, so we've done several investigation events in the building.

“Tonight we're doing some Inverness ghost stories for Halloween.

“The building has had reports. There have been reports of shadowy figures being seen moving in the building, noises, cold spots, people, even smells like pipe smoke and perfume.

“There’s a very famous organ within the church. During lockdown it was very important that that organ had to be played at least once a month.

“As the organists came to the door to unlock the building, they could hear the organ playing. Only when they opened the door did the music stop.”

Halloween is of great significance to the group, and to some, a source of great comfort.

Liam continued: “The belief is that Halloween is the night where the veil between the living and the dead is at its thinnest, so it's always a busy time of year for us, events-wise.

“There are people who are terrified at the thought of a ghost, but you also get others who are very intrigued and comforted by it. Some believe that their loved ones and ancestors are around them at Halloween.

“In some beliefs your ancestors come back.

“The paranormal in popular culture is very much based on the scary side of things. TV, movies, they paint that picture, but reality is something very different.”

After Halloween is over, things will not stop for Highland Paranormal, who are going to Strathpeffer for a paranormal convention, or ‘Paracon’.

Liam hopes to use this event to champion the Highlands

He said: “We don't just do Halloween. We're spooky all year round.

“The Paracon we're doing in November is very much a passion project. I've always wanted to do something in the Highlands. We have various guests from around the world coming to Inverness from America, New Zealand and Canada. When they meet up with us, they're blown away by the stories and history of the region.

“The Highlands is a very special, magical, and supernatural place in the eyes of many. Hopefully this Paracon can become a regular thing that we do on a yearly basis to celebrate the Highlands and its supernatural traditions.”
